messages:
Anya: Pushed a quick repro for a weird token jitter when we prefill + then append suffix on int8 sharded run. Repro: `python repro.py --model rwd-7b --ctx 12288 --quant int8 --shards 4` — diverges vs fp16 after ~4096 tokens. Anyone seen this?

Matt: Can you drop the remote logs or a short diff? stack traces would help but suspect KV mapping first.

Anya: Logs attached (snippet):
```
[2026-03-15T15:02:12Z] CacheShard[2]: read pos 4095 -> mapped 4095 OK
[2026-03-15T15:02:12Z] CacheShard[2]: read pos 4096 -> mapped 12288 ??? idx=-?
Mismatch at token idx 4097: expected "the", got "<|pad|>"
```

Cheng: That smells like an index wrap / shard-index remap bug. Prefill writes absolute positions but some read path might be doing modulo(window) + shard_offset incorrectly when quantized packing compresses indices.

Eva: I ran the repro with `--no-kv-rotation` and still get divergence but the pattern changed: repeating motif every 2048 tokens rather than immediate random pads. Baseline fp16 matches golden. int8 shows the repeat.

Jonah: @Cheng can you run with `--emit-kv-checks` (prints kv key hashes) to see whether distinct positions are colliding?

infra-bot: nightly longctx-int8-shard4 job queued: https://ci.redwood/infer/longctx/2156789 (build 7b-int8-shard4)

Cheng: Ran with `--emit-kv-checks`. Observed identical key hashes for different absolute positions:
```
pos 6144 -> hash 0x7af3
pos 12288 -> hash 0x7af3
pos 18432 -> hash 0x7af3
```
If true, that's a deterministic collision pattern (stride == 6144) which points to a modulo or bitshift being applied to the position before hashing.

Anya: I tried a quick patch to write absolute positions (avoid any post-mod normalization in prefill). With that, int8 run tracks fp16 through ~8192 tokens before diverging later — so it's reducing the problem but not fully fixed.

Eva: Also tried different shard counts (2 vs 4). Divergence point scales roughly with shard_count * 1024. So mapping math likely mixes shard index into position computation incorrectly.

Cheng: Hypothesis: when we pack indices for quantized kernels we do `idx_compressed = pos >> 4` to save space; for large pos this drops high bits and later code reconstructs idx with `(idx_compressed * 16) + (pos % 16)` but if we also add `shard_offset` without re-adding high bits, collisions happen. I'll add asserts to the mapping routine to catch reconstruction mismatches.

Anya: I'm putting together a small unit test that constructs positions across the full 12k window and asserts unique hashes after packing/unpacking. PR draft: rwd/runtime/kv_shard_map_test.py (local branch `prefill-kv-asserts`).

Jonah: Can we also add a regression in the longctx benchmark harness that runs the repro (fixed seed) at 12k and stores a checksum of the first 12 tokens after suffix append? If CI fails, it'll block merges.

Anya: Good call. Adding harness change + golden token checksum. Will update PR and ping.

Matt: Great. Assigning to @Cheng for root cause and to @Anya for the harness/PR. Once we have the assert firing locally, we can bisect the kernel switch that landed last week (rotary-interp kernel).

Eva: One more datapoint: running with `--quant int8 --kernel=fp16_fallback` reproduces fp16 behavior (no divergence). So the bug is likely in the int8 kernel path (packing/mapping) rather than data gen.

Anya: Thanks all — I'll post PR link when it's up. If anyone wants the repro script, it's in /rwd/experiments/longctx/repros/prefill_interleave.py

Matt: Thanks. Keeping this pinned until we have a failing CI test. :thumbsup:
